title: People keep saying "make the LLM read the filings." Nobody shows the pipeline. So I open-sourced mine.
author: Aggravating_War_4607
selftext:
Every "I made an LLM read the 10-K" post I've seen ends the same way: a screenshot, a do-it-yourself MCP setup, no pipeline. If the model really reads the filings, show me the whole path from filing to number. So here's mine, open-sourced: [https://github.com/wbaik/sapient.finance](https://github.com/wbaik/sapient.finance)  
  
  
The agents read the actual filings and come out with exactly three numbers, bear/base/bull: revenue CAGR, exit operating margin, exit multiple. Each one traces back to the filing — one surprise while building this was how much detail filings actually disclose about the business. The model never sees the price and never outputs a valuation. A fixed formula runs, and the result gets published as-is. The formulas are all in the repo.  
  
  
Example. INTU, EV/EBIT, 14 Jul 2026. It picked 7/11/15% growth, 27/31/34% margin, 18/24/30x. Base case works out to $591.67 a share. Price was $282.43.  
  
  
I've run valuations on 258 tickers so far.
